properties.statement:
`basis: measured` IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE CLAIM THE SCHEMA OFFERS AND THE ONLY ONE THAT DECAYS — and a CONSTRAINS edge carries no date, so a measurement is believed forever. music_graph F22, 2026-08-15; MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN THE SCHEMA HERE.

THEIR CASE: `con:frame-rate` recorded `cap:spectral-decomposition` contributing 6.9 fps with `basis: measured`, and `budget_report` duly reported a total of 6.9 against a 40 fps minimum. The true measured value was 55.06. The number was RIGHT WHEN TAKEN and had been wrong for days. Their framing is the one to keep: 'an estimate stays an estimate, but a measurement is a statement about a system at a moment.'

CONFIRMED IN `schema/core.yaml`: the CONSTRAINS edge declares exactly three properties — `note`, `contribution` (float) and `basis` (enum estimated | evidence | measured, default estimated). THERE IS NO DATE FIELD OF ANY KIND. So `budget_report` cannot say 'measured, but before the last 40 commits', and an agent reading it cannot tell a fresh measurement from a stale one. Nothing in the design records when the number was taken.

⭐ THE SHARP PART IS THAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HOLDS THIS DISCIPLINE ELSEWHERE, twice, and did not apply it here. `ver:evidence-quality` has a whole TIME axis: an accept dated after the check reports STALE, a re-run after the accept is current, and an undated side is UNKNOWN and counted rather than silently passed. `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` exists for precisely this reason, and its own description says a confirmation 'says nothing changed' so it is stored as a dated property. ⇒ DATING EVIDENCE IS ESTABLISHED DOCTRINE HERE, applied to Verification and to Artifact, and a budget contribution — the one number a KPP verdict rests on — has none.

THEIR SUGGESTION: a timestamp on the CONSTRAINS edge beside `basis`, and have `budget_report` age it against something — they propose the contributors' artifact checksums, which is the same trick `reconcile_artifacts` already uses to decide whether a file still matches.

⚠️ AND A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING IN THE SAME ENTRY, worth keeping because it cost them the time: for a MINIMUM budget the verdict went to `within` while a contributor was still `unstated`. For a MAXIMUM that would force `incomplete`, correctly, because a missing number can only make the total worse; for a minimum it can only make it better, so `within` is defensible. But the asymmetry is UNEXPLAINED IN THE PAYLOAD and 'looked like a bug until I reasoned it through'. The verdict is right and does not say why it is right.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a date belongs on the edge or on a separate observation node (the same question `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` answered by choosing the property, on the grounds that confirmations are high-frequency non-events); and whether ageing against artifact checksums is sound when a contribution can go stale without any file changing.
